2605.12279.text: Conjecture 1 (Albertson and Berman, 1976 [2]). Every simple undirected planar graph G on n vertices contains an induced forest of size at least \frac{n}{2} . Equivalently, Conjecture 1 states that every undirected planar graph G on n vertices has a feedback vertex set of size at most \frac{n}{2} . The best known general bound for Conjecture 1 is due to Borodin [4], who proved that every undirected planar graph admits an induced forest of size at least \frac{2n}{5} , in other words fvs(G)\leq\frac{3n}{5} . Better upper bounds for fvs are known depending on the girth (the length of a smallest cycle) and we summarize them in the second column of Table 1. The third column of this table shows the conjectured upper bounds, which are tight if true. While Conjecture 2 remains open in general, it was established by Li and Mohar [14] for planar oriented graphs without directed triangles.
